version.changelog:
cellcog 2.0.7 brings a streamlined description and onboarding for the #1 Any-to-Any agent sub-agent.

- Updated SKILL.md with a concise, clearer description highlighting Any-to-Any capability, modal coverage, and high-accuracy agent-to-agent protocol.
- Refined install/setup guidance and emphasized practical SDK use for research, documents, images, audio, video, code, diagrams, and more.
- Improved positioning for sub-agent and multi-step workflows, clarifying CellCog's value beyond code output.
- No code or API changes in this version; documentation only.

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: cellcog
Version: 2.0.7

The skill facilitates a bridge to an external service (cellcog.ai) that requires high-privilege access to the host system and the OpenClaw environment. Key indicators include instructions for the agent to read arbitrary local files via `<SHOW_FILE>` tags for remote processing, the requirement to enable sensitive gateway permissions (`sessions_send` and `sessions_list`) which allows the tool to interact with other active sessions, and the use of a background daemon for WebSocket communication. While these capabilities are aligned with the stated purpose of a multi-modal sub-agent, they create a significant surface for data exfiltration and session hijacking. These risks are documented in SKILL.md and involve the external domain cellcog.ai.

llm.summary: The skill's declared requirements and instructions align with its claim (an any-input→any-output agent) and it only asks for a single API key, but it is instruction-only so you should be aware that using it will upload any files you point it at and may require installing a PyPI package and enabling session delivery on your gateway.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (any-input → any-output agent) matches the skill's runtime instructions: it requires python3 and an API key to call the CellCog service and describes uploading/processing files and producing multi-format outputs. There are no unrelated binaries or unrelated environment variables requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs callers to include absolute local file paths inside <SHOW_FILE> tags so the SDK will include those file contents in requests. This is coherent with the skill's purpose (processing arbitrary files), but it means any file paths you provide will be read and transmitted to CellCog's service. It also documents a fire-and-forget mode that uses an OpenClaw notify_session_key and a background WebSocket/daemon for delivery, which requires enabling sessions_send on your gateway (a gateway configuration change). The instructions do not ask the agent to read unrelated env vars or system files beyond the files you explicitly tag, but users should understand the data-exfiltration implications of supplying file paths and enabling sessions_send.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill is instruction-only and provides a manual fallback 'pip install cellcog' if the Python package is missing. There is no automated install spec in the registry. Suggesting pip install is normal but does mean you may install third-party code from PyPI; that package would run locally and communicate with external servers. Verify the package and publisher before installing.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Only CELLCOG_API_KEY is required and is directly relevant to calling the remote CellCog API. No other secret environment variables or unrelated credentials are requested. The OpenClaw session key mentioned in examples is supplied as a parameter (notify_session_key), not as a required env var in the registry metadata.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not marked always:true and does not request system-wide persistence. It is allowed to be invoked autonomously (normal default) but doesn't request elevated or permanent privileges or to modify other skills' configs.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: What to consider before installing: 1) This skill will read and transmit any local files you include with <SHOW_FILE> tags — only provide files you are okay sending to cellcog.ai. 2) The SKILL.md suggests 'pip install cellcog' if missing; verify the PyPI package and publisher before installing and review what network calls the package makes. 3) Using the fire-and-forget mode requires enabling sessions_send on your gateway so CellCog can deliver results into OpenClaw sessions — enabling that feature gives external deliveries into your sessions, so enable only if you trust CellCog and have reviewed gateway implications. 4) Create/limit the CELLCOG_API_KEY to minimal privileges and monitor billing and data usage. 5) If you need higher assurance, ask the vendor for an audited SDK/package URL (e.g., official GitHub release) and a data-processing/privacy statement; test with non-sensitive files first.
llm.findings: [no_code_files_to_scan] expected: The regex scanner found nothing because this is an instruction-only skill (SKILL.md only). This is expected; absence of findings is not proof of safety — review the instructions carefully.
